sections.label: FIMA Bill harmonises MAS investigative powers
sections.summary: The FIMA Bill will harmonise and enhance MAS' investigative powers across six MAS-administered Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The Financial Institutions (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill (FIMA Bill), will harmonise and enhance MAS' investigative powers across six Acts, namely the Financial Advisors Act 2001, the Financial Services and Markets Act 2022, the Insurance Act 1966, the Payment Services Act 2019, the Securities and Futures Act 2001 and the Trust Companies Act 2005, collectively, the MAS-administered Acts.

sections.label: Investigation powers gaps across Acts
sections.summary: Some investigation powers under the SFA and FAA are not available in the FSMA, Insurance Act, Payment Services Act and Trust Companies Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Such enforcement actions are not possible without MAS conducting rigorous investigations of suspected violations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: However, some of the investigation powers available to MAS under the Securities and Futures Act (SFA) and the Financial Advisers Act (FAA) are not available in the other MAS-administered Acts, specifically the Financial Services and Markets Act (FSMA), Insurance Act (IA), Payment Services Act (PS Act) and Trust Companies Act (TCA).

sections.label: FIMA Bill closes investigation power gaps
sections.summary: The FIMA Bill will close gaps by enhancing and making consistent investigation powers across all MAS-administered Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The FIMA Bill will close these gaps by enhancing and making consistent the investigation powers across all of the MAS-administered Acts.

sections.label: Transfer of evidence to MAS
sections.summary: The FIMA Bill will replace provisions with power for Police or law enforcement agencies to transfer evidence to MAS for regulatory actions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The FIMA Bill will replace these provisions with the power for the Police or other law enforcement agencies to transfer evidence to MAS, for the purpose of taking regulatory actions in respect of any misconduct under the MAS-administered Acts if such transfer is in the public interest.

sections.label: MAS directions on unregulated businesses
sections.summary: The FIMA Bill will empower MAS to issue legally binding directions to CMSL holders and representatives on unregulated businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The FIMA Bill will empower MAS to issue legally binding directions to CMSL holders and their representatives in relation to their conduct of unregulated businesses, to mitigate risks posed to its regulated businesses.

sections.label: Approval for external auditors
sections.summary: The FIMA Bill will require such entities to obtain MAS' approval annually for appointing their external auditors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The FIMA Bill will introduce the requirement for such entities to obtain MAS' approval for the appointment of their external auditors on an annual basis.

sections.label: MAS warrantless entry powers
sections.summary: The Bill grants the MAS powers including the power to enter without a warrant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Specifically, the Bill grants the MAS powers including the power to enter without a warrant.

sections.label: Protecting legitimate institutions, stricter enforcement
sections.summary: The measures protect legitimate institutions from undue anxiety while guaranteeing stricter, more expeditious enforcement, unlike Hong Kong which has not enacted similar legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is essential to emphasise how these measures will protect legitimate institutions from undue anxiety, while simultaneously guaranteeing stricter and more expeditious enforcement actions that ultimately serve the interests of bona fide institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Such a measure is not commonplace in other financial hubs, such as Hong Kong, which has not enacted similar legislation even in its recent tightening of financial regulations.

sections.label: Court warrant for seizing evidence
sections.summary: A Court warrant is still necessary for seizing evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Moreover, it is important to note that a Court warrant is still necessary for seizing evidence.

sections.label: FIMA Bill amends various acts
sections.summary: The FIMA Bill amends various acts to enhance MAS' investigative powers, regulate additional business activities, clarify reprimand authority and improve financial institution governance, with stricter licensing for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The FIMA Bill aims to amend various acts to enhance MAS' investigative powers, regulate additional business activities, clarify MAS' authority to reprimand formerly regulated persons for past misconduct and improve the governance and control of financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For businesses, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the financial sector, the Bill introduces stricter licensing and compliance requirements; which, while increasing administrative work, enhances trust within the business community.

sections.label: MAS enhanced regulatory tools, clarification sought
sections.summary: The Bill gives MAS enhanced tools and flexibility to regulate financial institutions, and the speaker supports it but asks how MAS will synergise information with Suspicious Transaction Reports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It aims to provide MAS with enhanced tools and flexibility to effectively regulate and supervise financial institutions operating under its jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I therefore support the Bill, but I have few points to clarify with the Minister： With the enhanced power, how does MAS intend to synergise the information that it collects and harmonise, with the Suspicious Transaction Reports filed with the Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office?

sections.label: MAS investigative powers expanded
sections.summary: The amendments expand MAS' investigative powers under five pieces of legislation and provide new powers under one additional piece.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments will expand MAS' investigative powers under five pieces of legislation and provide MAS new investigative powers under one additional piece of legislation.

sections.label: No excuse for disclosure
sections.summary: New section 89(1) states a person is not excused from disclosing information because it might incriminate the person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 89(1) provides that a person is not excused from disclosing information on the ground that the disclosure of information might tend to incriminate the person.

sections.label: Legal counsel must give name
sections.summary: New section 89(3) requires a legal counsel refusing to disclose privileged communications to still give the person's name and address.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the new section 89(3), a legal counsel who refuses to disclose privileged communications must still give the name and address of the person to whom the privileged communication was made.

sections.label: MAS investigative powers and privilege
sections.summary: MAS inserted a provision stating its investigative powers do not require disclosure of information subject to legal privilege.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: For instance, in response to feedback that it was unclear whether MAS' investigative powers would override legal professional privilege, MAS inserted a new provision to state that MAS' exercise of its investigative powers does not require a person to disclose any information subject to legal privilege.

sections.label: MAS cannot compel privileged communication
sections.summary: MAS will not compel the identified person to produce the privileged communication, as its investigation powers do not override legal professional privilege.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS will not compel or force the person identified to produce the privileged communication to MAS, as MAS' investigation powers do not override legal professional privilege.

sections.label: MAS sharing with STRO
sections.summary: Because STRO is part of the Commercial Affairs Department, MAS can share information with STRO for criminal investigations or proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Since STRO is part of Singapore Police Force's Commercial Affairs Department, MAS will be able to share information with STRO as needed to pursue such criminal investigations or proceedings.

sections.label: FIMA Bill and MAS information
sections.summary: The FIMA Bill will enable MAS to be more effective in obtaining information about a suspected failure of a licensed payment service provider.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The FIMA Bill will enable MAS to be more effective in obtaining information regarding a suspected failure of a licensed payment service provider to comply with its obligations under the PS Act.

sections.label: MAS notice before warrantless entry
sections.summary: MAS must give two days' notice before entering premises without a warrant, except in two stated situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS will have to give two days’ notice before entering premises without a warrant, unless: one, there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that the premises are, or have been, occupied by a suspect; or two, MAS has taken all reasonably practicable steps to give such notice to the occupier of the premises, but has not been able to do so.

sections.label: MAS power over digital evidence
sections.summary: The amendments clarify that MAS can require production of and access to digital evidence, including cloud-stored evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The proposed amendments make clear that MAS has the power to require a person to produce digital evidence and to access digital evidence, including evidence stored in a cloud.

sections.label: Directions to CMSL holders
sections.summary: The amendment lets MAS issue directions to CMSL holders as a class and to individual CMSL holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: With the amendment, MAS will be able to issue directions to CMSL holders as a class as well as to individual CMSL holders.

sections.label: Consultation on unregulated financial products
sections.summary: MAS will consult the industry on the proposed list of unregulated financial products and standards, with a transition period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS will conduct a public consultation to seek industry feedback on the proposed list of unregulated financial products and standards and will provide an appropriate transition period for industry to adopt these standards.

sections.label: Electronic service with prior consent
sections.summary: Documents may be served electronically only with the person's prior consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Relevant documents may only be served through electronic service with a person’s prior consent to ensure that such documents are brought to the attention of the person as needed.

sections.label: Factors in MAS enforcement action
sections.summary: MAS would consider listed factors when assessing action against a financial institution, and the amendments aim to enable more effective supervision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In assessing whether to take action against a financial institution, MAS would consider the nature of the information submitted, the significance of the error, the robustness of the financial institution's internal controls and processes, the frequency of erroneous submissions to MAS and the circumstances leading to the breach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The amendments are necessary to enable MAS to supervise FIs and uphold the regulatory regime under its purview more effectively in a rapidly-evolving financial system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: It signals our commitment to maintain the high standards of integrity and trust in Singapore's financial system.
